student_integration.language_course_details: A Romanian language course is offered but is only held if at least 10 students enroll and interest is queried during the orientation meeting.

universities_fit_text: Strasbourg offers a medium-sized, walkable city with strong historical core and museums (good for culture/nightlife) and winters that are chilly but not extreme. ECAM is a smaller engineering school with a more unified, campus-like student experience (easy to make friends) but not a massive Erasmus party hub. Estimated semester cost: ~$6,000 (Western/Southern Europe typical), within your $9k cap.

University of Cyprus sits on a compact campus near Nicosia, giving a relatively unified student bubble and easier social integration; Nicosia offers historical sites and mild Mediterranean winters. Nightlife exists but is smaller than big European hubs. Estimated semester cost: ~$6,000 (Southern Europe tail), comfortably under $9k.

DTU has a strong enclosed campus (Lyngby) with legendary campus bars and very active student life — excellent for making friends. Copenhagen gives world-class museums and nightlife but winters are colder and cost of living is high. Estimated semester cost: ~$9,500 (Northern Europe high), which exceeds or pushes your $9k comfort threshold.

Centrale Marseille is in a large Mediterranean port city—excellent museums, historical neighborhoods, nightlife and mild winters. Campus life is less of an enclosed college-town bubble (more urban/integrated), so making friends requires more initiative. Estimated semester cost: ~$6,000 (Western/Southern Europe), under $9k.

CentraleSupélec (Saclay/Gif region) offers an elite, enclosed campus culture that facilitates friend-making and strong student organizations (more 'closed' grande école bubble). Proximity to Paris gives world-class museums, nightlife and cultural sites. Costs near Paris are higher than provincial France—estimated semester cost: ~$8,500–$9,000 (Western Europe, Paris premium), near your maximum.

Anhalt UAS is in smaller towns with campus-like, close-knit student life (great for making friends) and very low costs. Cultural offerings are more modest than big cities but there are niche museums (e.g., Bauhaus in Dessau). Winters are cooler but not extreme. Estimated semester cost: ~$4,000–$5,000 (Germany, small-town outlier) — very affordable.

Jena is a genuine university town with a compact, student-centered feel — ideal for a unified campus experience and easy friend-making. Good regional culture, museums and manageable nightlife; winters are colder but not extreme. Estimated semester cost: ~$3,500–$4,500 (Eastern/cheaper German city), very budget friendly relative to your $9k cap.

Hannover combines a sizable student population with campus pockets but is more of a mid-size city (moderate ease of meeting people). Cultural amenities and museums exist, winters moderate-cold. Estimated semester cost: ~$5,500 (Western Europe/Germany average), comfortably under $9k.

Erlangen (with nearby Nuremberg) is a classic German student city with strong campus feel in Erlangen, lively student societies and an approachable social scene—good for making friends. The region offers museums, historical architecture and decent nightlife; winters are moderate. Estimated semester cost: ~$5,500–$6,000, under your $9k limit.

TUM has strong campus elements (Garching) but also a big-city Munich presence; it’s social and well connected to student groups. Munich offers world-class museums, historic sites and nightlife, but winters are colder than Mediterranean options and cost of living is high. Estimated semester cost: ~$8,000–$9,000 (upper Western Europe), near your ceiling.

Polimi is an Erasmus/ international nightlife magnet with outstanding museums and cultural life in Milan, but it is decentralized within a large metropolis rather than a single unified residential campus (less ideal for your desire for a compact campus). Winters are mild-to-cool. Estimated semester cost: ~$6,500 (Western Europe/Milan), under $9k.

Iasi is a textbook student city with a compact, social campus culture—excellent for making friends and immersive campus life. Rich historical sites, museums and a lively student nightlife; winters are colder than Mediterranean but generally tolerable. Estimated semester cost: ~$2,500–$3,500 (Eastern Europe low), well below your $9k cap.

ORT in Montevideo offers an urban-but-manageable campus feel in a mid-sized coastal capital with good cultural life, museums and relaxed nightlife; southern hemisphere winters are mild. Costs in Uruguay are comparatively low for an exchange. Estimated semester cost: ~$4,000 (Latin America), comfortably within budget.

PoliTO is in Torino, a culturally rich city with excellent museums and history and more of a cohesive student city feel than Milan—better aligned with a traditional campus desire though still urban. Nightlife is good; winters can be cool. Estimated semester cost: ~$5,500–$6,000 (Western/Southern Europe), under $9k.

TU Berlin is embedded in a sprawling global city (big commuter feel) — excellent museums, nightlife and culture but not a single unified residential campus, so it’s less aligned with your desire for an enclosed college-town. Winters are moderate. Estimated semester cost: ~$6,000 (Western Europe/Berlin), within your $9k budget.
